title: Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle ends the War of the Austrian Succession
summary: Britain, France and the Dutch Republic signed peace at Aachen, later joined by the other powers, largely restoring conquests on both sides.
reason: Eight years of war over the succession of Maria Theresa had become costly for all sides without a clear winner.
significance: Prussia kept Silesia, and the unresolved rivalries led to the Seven Years' War.
